answer: In PoA, each agent’s identity is bound to a Wesolowski VDF requiring a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings. Since every square depends on the preceding result, GPUs cannot divide one proof among parallel clone simulations; creating more identities proportionally increases elapsed wall-clock time. Consequently, knoll, ledge, and terrace nodes encounter the same physical bottleneck, making Sybil attacks economically and temporally infeasible.
